test_title: PYST 56: RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I - GA (Held On: 09 Sept, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Which of the following Directive Principles reflects Gandhian ideology?

options.text: Separation of judiciary from the executive

solution:
The correct answer is __**Organisation of village panchayats**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Directive Principle of **Organisation of village panchayats** is mentioned under Article 40 of the Indian Constitution.
 
• It reflects **Gandhian ideology**, emphasizing decentralized governance and empowerment of rural areas.
 
• Mahatma Gandhi believed in the concept of Gram Swaraj, advocating for self-reliant villages as the foundation of India's democracy.
 
• The idea promotes **local self-governance**, enabling villages to manage their affairs independently and democratically.
 
• The establishment of village panchayats aims to ensure participatory democracy, grassroots development, and social justice.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Equal pay for equal work:**

 
 
• This principle is enshrined under Article 39(d) of the Constitution of India.
 
• It falls under the category of economic principles rather than Gandhian ideology.
 
• It aims to promote equality in wages irrespective of gender, ensuring social and economic justice in employment.
 
 
 
• **Uniform civil code:**
 
 
• The concept of a Uniform Civil Code is laid out under Article 44 of the Indian Constitution.
 
• It calls for a common set of laws governing personal matters such as marriage, divorce, inheritance, and adoption across all religions.
 
• This principle reflects liberal and modern ideas rather than Gandhian ideology.
 
 
 
• **Separation of judiciary from the executive:**
 
 
• This principle is mentioned under Article 50 of the Indian Constitution.
 
• It advocates for the independence of the judiciary from the executive branch to uphold the rule of law and justice.
 
• This reflects administrative and legal principles rather than Gandhian thought.
